cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Observability is being able to explain what a system is doing from the signals it emits: metrics, logs and traces. Metrics say something is wrong and when, traces show which hop was slow, and structured logs tied by a correlation ID show why.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Define reliability as SLIs and SLOs with an error budget (100 percent minus SLO). Alert on user-facing symptoms like error rate or latency, not every cause. Use percentiles, not averages. Avoid high-cardinality labels like user_id. Traces connect across services through context propagation (traceparent).

questions.a: SLI is the measurement, SLO the internal target, SLA the external promise, usually looser than the SLO.

questions.q: Why is a user_id metric label dangerous?
questions.a: Each value creates a new time series, exhausting memory. Put user detail in logs and traces.

questions.q: Why alert on symptoms rather than causes?
questions.a: Symptoms map to user pain and catch unexpected causes; cause alerts multiply and cause alert fatigue.
